question: In a certain code language, 'MERCHANT’ is written as 'NFSCHCPV' and 'INTERIOR' is written as 'JOUERKQT'. How will 'JUNCTION' be written in that language?
solution:
Alphabet table:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b1ef5af07dc7cdface0347994bbc6f824cbda2bac27bcab0cb4cf07968dfa00.png] 

The pattern followed is:

For, 'MERCHANT’ is written as 'NFSCHCPV'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c34afa0ad137532c8b0eb7d695a0f2e77d62de924ee487d2fce7353487725788.png] 

For, 'INTERIOR' is written as 'JOUERKQT'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1d60498cf84195fb47277b180dc22c48cc6f7a5de24fff78457c36aae58663d.png] 

Similarly, for 'JUNCTION'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5c38cf7909670ab86959f0e86837311ff0fe66891f8d9be3d86c612a12cf77c.png] 

So, 'JUNCTION' will be written as 'KVOCTKQP'. 

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.
